sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. Austronesian languages: Milne Bay and adjacent islands (Milne Bay Province). In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 441-523. Pacific Linguistics C-39
sources.note: Para 84 'Stress' p. 475 is Papuan-Tip-Cluster-wide only: penultimate vowel lengthening in Dobu; stress phonemic in Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima; 'In all of the languages of PTC it seems that stress is predictable within certain word-classes, notably kinship nouns and verbs' (shifts one syllable toward the end under suffixation); Dobu 3-syllable nouns often initial. Sewa Bay is not named; it appears only in para 43 (pp. 457-458, seven diverse dialects, cognate matrix) and pronoun/affix tables.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David. 1992. Language change on Fergusson and Normanby Islands, Milne Bay Province, Papua New Guinea. In Tom Dutton (ed.), Culture change, language change: case studies from Melanesia, 27-47. Pacific Linguistics C-120. DOI 10.15144/PL-C120.27
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6 'Phonology changes' (pp. 37-38) treats only glottal stop, h and labialised consonants (Sewa has no glottal stop and no h); sec. 8 gives Pwanapwana-dialect Sewa word lists 1964/1982/1989; 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in the text.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David. 1992. Using grammatical data to determine language relationships in Fergusson and Normanby Island languages of the Papuan Tip cluster. Language and Linguistics in Melanesia 23: 119-138.
sources.note: Grammatical-similarity study (29 clauses, 85 contrastive features); Sewa Bay in the vocabulary/grammar similarity matrices (e.g. SEW-DOB 67, SEW-BUN 49/52); only phonological remark is nonphonemic [dh]~[j]~[dark l] fluctuation written <y>; no stress or tone statement on the pages viewed (pp.119-121 rendered as images; PDF has no text, rest is clause data, not scanned under the window rule).

sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. History of research in Austronesian languages: Milne Bay Province. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 157-170. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU (hdl 1885/252993).
sources.note: No phonology of Sewa Bay. A research-history/bibliography chapter: it states that for Sewa Bay nothing is recorded except survey material (Lithgow & Staalsen 1965, 21 pp. with maps; Parlier, Austing, Lithgow et al. 1973 'Languages of the East Papua Region', SIL work-book, Ukarumpa); the only stress remark in the section concerns Sudest, Nimowa and Misima ('non-predictable stress'), not Sewa Bay. Anthropologists' language documentation listed for Normanby is Roheim (Duau) only; Catholic mission grammar noted only for Kurada (Fr Moore 1961).
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study
